issue.title: SQL: Improve the test coverage of the Verifier

labels.name: Team:QL (Deprecated)
labels.description: Meta label for query languages team

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Increases the already high line coverage to 98%+ (couple of trivial checks and 
failure reporting methods will be left out).

The reason for increasing the test coverage on the Verifier
is to gain extra confidence that later moving rules between the
Analyzer and Optimizer won't break any current functionality,
won't turn current checks effectively no-op.

Loosely related, but fixing https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/69758 
might require moving the `PruneSubqueryAlias` rule between the Analyzer 
and Optimizer, hence the Verifier might see an extra `SubqueryAlias` node
in the plan tree (and would think that some checks should not apply).

issue.title: SQL: Implement filter push-down for GROUP BYs

labels.name: Team:QL (Deprecated)
labels.description: Meta label for query languages team

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Previously we were not able to execute queries like the one below,
where we filter on the groupings of the `Aggregate`s. The reasons are
the limitations of the `bucket_selector`s `bucket_path` [0] that cannot
filter on non-numerical keys.

The implemented optimization transforms the following query:

```sql
SELECT i, a
FROM (
     SELECT int as i, AVG(float) as a
     FROM test
     GROUP BY int
) WHERE i = 1 AND a > 1
```

To one equivalent to this:

```sql
SELECT i, a
FROM (
     SELECT int as i, AVG(float) as a
     FROM test
     WHERE int = 1
     GROUP BY int
) WHERE a > 1
```

The latter query can be translated to Query DSL.

The change also makes it possible to use a query with HAVING in a
subselect with filters in the outer query. We can have multiple levels
of queries on a single GROUP BY with filters on multiple levels. At
the end the filters will be collapsed, the conditions on the
aggregates will transformed into an equivalent of HAVING, while the
conditions on groupings will be pushed below the GROUP BY query.

Note: because of the limitation [0] mentioned above
(sub-)conditions that use expressions both on groupings and aggregates
of the GROUP BY and unsplittable (groupings and aggregates are not in
separate child of a conjunction) cannot be handled.

For example the following query will fail with a VerifierException:

```sql
SELECT *
FROM (
     SELECT int, count(*) as cnt
     FROM test
     GROUP BY int
)
WHERE int > 2 OR cnt > 1
```

because the `int > 2 OR cnt > 1` filters both on the groupings (`int >
2`) and the aggregates (`cnt > 1` that translates to `count(*) > 1`).

Note: Queries like

```sql
SELECT MAX(int) FROM test WHERE MAX(int) > 10
```

are still not allowed (HAVING should be used).

Also fixes #69758, by making the queries work utilizing the filter
push-down, but note that there are changes in the
`EXPLAIN (PLAN ANALYZED)` outputs (`SubqueryAlias` node appears).

[0] https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/23874

issue.title: SQL: Introduce dedicated node for HAVING declaration

labels.name: Team:QL (Deprecated)
labels.description: Meta label for query languages team

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Currently HAVING is modeled as a Filter - while this works well
conceptually, it leads to false positives when validation correct usage
of HAVING (only on aggregate functions or grouped expressions).
This occurs because there's no way to detect whether a filter was
declared as a WHERE or HAVING call - the existing heuristic works in
basic queries but fails when dealing with subqueries.

This PR addresses the issue by introducing a dedicated HAVING node that,
through its definition, clearly disambiguate between regular Filter
(WHERE) and aggregated one (HAVING).

Fix #69758
